How do I resolve conflicting signals on TSLA into month-end: MACD is bullish but price is below the 200-day?
column2: TSLA bullish MACD below the 200-day is a counter-trend signal at best.

column1: Exxon Mobil is 37% of my portfolio. Should I rebalance?
column2: With XOM at 37% of the book, one earnings report can move the whole portfolio.

column1: What does a MACD bullish crossover on QQQ mean for daily charts?
column2: A MACD bullish crossover on QQQ means the fast line crossed above the slow line — momentum is turning up on the daily chart.

column1: How do I read a MACD bearish crossover on SPY (daily timeframe)?
column2: A MACD bearish crossover on SPY means the fast line crossed below the slow line — momentum is turning down on the daily chart.

column1: What is the Kelly bet size for a 45% win rate and 3:1 payoff?
column2: Full Kelly for a 45% win rate at 3:1 payoff is 26.7% of capital, but full Kelly assumes your estimates are exact.

column1: Is missing earnings but cuts guidance a signal on TSLA?
column2: When Tesla misses and cuts guidance, the first move is down and gap risk is real.

column1: Would you keep TSLA unchanged in a portfolio today?
column2: Verdict on TSLA: HOLD — trend and momentum disagree (price strong, RSI cooling), and the risk/reward at the current level is not clearly favorable.

column1: Is beating earnings and raises guidance a signal on TSLA?
column2: A beat with raised guidance on TSLA is the strongest signal in the set: the initial pop rewards holders and the trend typically extends.

column1: What does MSFT touching the upper band of the Bollinger Bands on the daily chart tell me?
column2: MSFT tagging the upper Bollinger Band on the daily chart is statistically stretched.

column1: How should I trade XOM at the Bollinger lower band on a weekly chart?
column2: XOM tagging the lower Bollinger Band on the weekly chart is stretched to the downside.

column1: How do I read a MACD bullish crossover on JPM (weekly timeframe)?
column2: A MACD bullish crossover on JPM means the fast line crossed above the slow line — momentum is turning up on the weekly chart.

column1: Why is JPM a buy here?
column2: Verdict on JPM: BUY.

column1: TSLA beats earnings but cuts guidance — how should I read it?
column2: When Tesla beats but cuts guidance, the pop often fades within days: the durable signal is guidance, not the print.

column1: How do I resolve conflicting signals on MSFT at the highs: price is at resistance with a high RSI?
column2: MSFT at resistance with a high RSI is a poor place to add: entries belong at support or after a confirmed breakout, not into a ceiling with stretched momentum.

column1: What does QQQ touching the lower band of the Bollinger Bands on the daily chart tell me?
column2: QQQ tagging the lower Bollinger Band on the daily chart is stretched to the downside.

column1: How do I resolve conflicting signals on SPY with volume rising: MACD is bullish but price is below the 200-day?
column2: SPY bullish MACD below the 200-day is a counter-trend signal at best.

column1: Thoughts on holding 4 stocks?
column2: 4 positions is workable if each has a written thesis and a stop.

column1: How tight should an ATR-based stop be on MSFT?
column2: An ATR stop on MSFT sits about 2 ATRs below entry: wide enough to survive normal noise, tight enough to cap the loss at a known multiple of daily volatility.

column1: What is the Kelly bet size for a 63% win rate and 1.5:1 payoff?
